text:
rachel: heads-up — AcmeChat (hosted-prod us-west-2) just opened a support ticket: p95 ~2.4s -> p99 spikes up to ~12s for text-generation. They attached traces showing GPU stalls and a bunch of OOMs. Started ~02:58 UTC, right after the latest runtime deploy.

sam: pinging eng-runtime oncall @mia — can you take a look? they flagged 15% error rate and a bunch of timeouts.

mia: I'm on it. grabbing logs from the node group now. do we have the deploy id?

rachel: deploy-bot shows `deploy/eng-runtime/20260315.0257` completed at 02:57:12 UTC. attached to the ticket: sampling of user requests and one raw request payload that repros.

javier: quick skim of metrics — GPU mem usage climbs steadily for sessions from that customer, then we see `cudaMalloc` failures and long GC-like stalls in the allocator. p99 correlates with `kv_cache_size` growth per session.

mia: pasting the hot logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T02:59:03Z] WARN gpu0: cudaError(2) out of memory while allocating 512MB
[2026-03-15T02:59:03Z] ERROR runtime::allocator: allocation failed, trying fallback
[2026-03-15T02:59:04Z] INFO kv_cache: client=acme: session_id=abc123 appended 1.2GB; total_kv=3.8GB
[2026-03-15T02:59:04Z] WARN runtime::batcher: increased latency p99=11.6s
```

mia: full stack shows allocator fragmentation + KV growth per request. looks like we didn't cap the per-session KV retention in the new variant.

priya: known risk — the new model variant keeps KV for longer to support long-chat semantics. we updated the LRU threshold in the config but maybe the flag didn't roll out to all nodes.

sam: can you repro locally? javier, any quick repro steps?

javier: yes: minimal repro (worked on a small test infra):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-long-context","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":1024,"history_tokens":15000}'
```
If you send a long history (12-18k tokens) and then several follow-ups quickly, `total_kv` grows and allocator can't compact quickly; on GPU with smaller free blocks fragmentation leads to `cudaMalloc` OOMs while the process is still holding 60-80% of GPU mem in small free fragments.

mia: repro on staging confirmed. it's fragmentation + KV retention per session. two immediate mitigation options: 1) revert the variant rollout to the previous model with conservative KV retention, or 2) apply an on-node hotfix that enforces aggressive KV eviction when free contiguous memory < X.

rachel: customer needs immediate relief — can we switch their routing to a smaller-compatible variant until we ship a fix?

sam: yes, routing change is quick. Priya, can you open a routing override for AcmeChat to `rwd-chat-ltq` for the next 24h? use safe-fallback policy.

priya: opening PM request now and tagging @ops. id: RM-4472. will apply override in ~5 mins.

deploy-bot: scheduled route override applied to customer=acme, target_model=rwd-chat-ltq, expire=2026-03-16T03:00:00Z

mia: parallel mitigation we should push: a small allocator tuning that reduces slab fragmentation and forces coalescing on free if contiguous < 256MB, and add a per-session KV upper bound (e.g., 2GB) with best-effort eviction. That should avoid OOMs while preserving most long-chat behavior.

javier: I prototyped allocator tweak — adding `--alloc-coalesce-threshold=268435456` and `--enable-kv-evict=true --kv-evict-target=2147483648` seems to stop the OOMs in staging. perf impact: +1-2% CPU for coalescing.

mia: can we ship a hotfix release containing the alloc param and KV guard? we can do a canary to 5% first.

sam: schedule a hotfix patch release. Eng-runtime to push canary to us-west-2 behind a rollout flag. If green at 5% for 30m, rollout to 50% then 100%.

rachel: also please document the remediation steps in support ticket so CS can communicate to AcmeChat. They asked for root cause analysis and timeline.

priya: adding notes to ticket: route override applied, canary hotfix planned, ETA 1h for initial canary.

javier: follow-up notes from profiling: the problem surface was a combination of 1) unbounded session KV retention when `history_tokens` > 10k, and 2) a memory allocator that tends to fragment under rapid many small allocations/free cycles. Both needed to be addressed to fix p99 reliably.

mia: postmortem plan: short-term: route override + hotfix (allocator coalesce + KV eviction). medium-term: add unit tests for KV retention limits, integration tests that simulate KV churn, and a memory-defrag metric to alert earlier.

sam: I created an incident doc in /incidents/INC-2026-03-15-acme-kv-oom (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-03-15-acme-kv-oom). please add your notes.

rachel: thanks team. once hotfix is live and metrics look stable for 2h, I'll update the customer and close the support ticket.

mia: quick checklist before canary:
- build hotfix image with `--alloc-coalesce-threshold=268435456` and `--enable-kv-evict=true --kv-evict-target=2147483648`
- smoke test on staging with long-history stream
- deploy to us-west-2 canary 5% with route override still active for AcmeChat
- monitor p95/p99 and `cudaMalloc` errors, `total_kv` per-session

javier: I'll own the build and smoke tests. deploying now to canary registry tag `eng-runtime:hotfix-20260315-a`.

observability-bot: ALERT closed: cudaMalloc OOM rate decreased from 0.8% -> 0.02% in staging after hotfix (smoke run).

rachel: great. keep me posted on canary results. thanks all. :heart:
